☕ THE LEAD

The creator economy just solidified its place squarely in your paid media budget, not just the "influencer marketing" line item. A new report this week found that paid media backing creator content now makes up nearly half of the entire creator marketing category. We're talking $52 billion of the estimated $116 billion global influencer market this year, and it’s projected to grow twice as fast as overall ad spending over the next five years. This isn't just brands dipping their toes; it's a fundamental shift where creator-generated content is being treated as a scalable, performance-driven ad format. If your team is still silo-ing "influencer marketing" from "paid media," you're missing out on a massive, proven channel that's delivering real ROI. The takeaway: stop thinking of creators as just "influencers" and start integrating their content directly into your paid strategy. [S5][S14]

📣 QUICK HITS

**Maker's Mark gets a modern refresh, keeps the red wax.**
The bourbon brand is updating its visual identity, putting its iconic hand-dipped red wax top front and center. It's a smart move to modernize while leaning into a distinctive brand asset, especially as the bourbon market faces slowing growth. [S6]

**Meta tries (again) to launch a messaging app for teens.**
The company rolled out 'Direct,' designed to expand Instagram DMs to a separate platform. Sound familiar? It's almost identical to a Direct app Meta launched (and shuttered) in 2017. Maybe they're hoping the second time's the charm with a new generation of users. [S27]

**Google gives its AI Search feature an incognito mode.**
You can now have conversations in AI Mode without them cluttering your search history or influencing future recommendations. A nod to privacy, or an admission that sometimes you just want to ask AI weird stuff without judgment? Probably both. [S2]

**GTA VI launch is a full-blown real-world takeover.**
With Grand Theft Auto VI launching tomorrow, Rockstar Games is going all out, taking over iconic spots in Miami and beyond. This isn't just a game launch; it's an immersive brand experience, showing how to build anticipation beyond digital hype. [S1][S12][S69]

🎯 THE PMM DESK

**2027 Business Trends Report highlights shifting priorities.**
A new report from Product Marketing Alliance, based on millions of surveys from over 260,000 organizations, pinpoints what businesses were asking about most in 2026 and where their focus is headed for 2027. For PMMs, this is gold for validating market needs, identifying emerging pain points, and ensuring your product strategy and messaging align with what buyers actually care about. [S3]

**PMMs need to elevate content beyond AI's baseline.**
An article from PMA argues that while AI has raised the *floor* on content creation, PMMs now need to focus on raising the *ceiling*. This means moving past generic, AI-generated drafts to create truly strategic, differentiated, and insightful content that cuts through the noise and delivers unique value. [S11]

🧠 PMM 101

**The concept:** Raising the Content Ceiling
**What it is:** With AI making basic content creation (drafts, summaries, boilerplate copy) accessible to everyone, "raising the content ceiling" means focusing on creating truly strategic, differentiated, and impactful content that AI can't replicate. It's about adding unique insights, deep market understanding, a distinct brand voice, and a compelling narrative that resonates specifically with your target audience.
**Why it matters:** In a world flooded with AI-generated mediocrity, your product's story needs to stand out.
**See it today:** The Product Marketing Alliance article explicitly calls out this challenge, noting that PMMs are uniquely positioned to infuse AI-generated content with strategic value. [S11]
**Try it:** Take a recent piece of content (like a product brief or a blog post draft) that you might have used AI to start, and brainstorm three specific, unique points of view or insights *only your team* could add to elevate it beyond a generic output.

🧩 PRODUCT CORNER

**Google is forcing Android apps to support foldables.**
Starting April 2027, Android developers will be required to meet a "Tier 3 - Adaptive ready" standard for foldables, meaning apps must fill the available display area without letterboxing or compatibility modes. This is a big move to ensure a consistent, high-quality user experience across a growing device category, pushing developers to prioritize design for flexible form factors or risk reduced visibility on Google Play. [S40]

🔧 TOOL DROP

**Microsoft IQ** — Give AI agents a shared understanding of your business. [S39][S106]
Best for: Enterprises looking to deploy multiple AI agents that need to work together and access consistent, up-to-date business knowledge.
Free tier: No (likely enterprise pricing)
Honest take: This could be genuinely useful for large organizations struggling with siloed AI tools. The "shared understanding" angle is key to making AI agents truly productive, moving beyond individual task automation to coordinated intelligence. If it works as advertised, it's a big step for enterprise AI adoption.

⚡ SPEED ROUND

✨ Target's holiday momentum: toys, games, and electronics are up almost 27%, while home and apparel are falling short. [S20]
🛒 Instacart is back for its third consecutive Super Bowl ad, showing continued big-brand commitment to the event. [S21]
💅 Snapchat found 84% of its users feel connected to the luxury universe through social media. [S26]
🤖 Over a third of Gen Z reports relying on AI for friendship, but this group also faces higher odds of loneliness. [S87]
💸 Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress confirmed the company is abandoning China after Jensen Huang's ouster, a potentially massive financial hit. [S92]
🗣️ Sam Altman warned against a future where AI, not humans, makes the decisions, acknowledging the challenge of keeping advanced models under human control. [S48]
